I'm now looking at receipt_0016.jpg more carefully, where the line "Rounded Total (RM): 13.50" doesn't cleanly fit the "TOTAL RM" pattern since the RM is parenthetical rather than adjacent to TOTAL—I need to see how the actual OCR output formats this before deciding how my matching rule should handle it.

But receipt_0151's total line, "Total Sales (Inclusive GST) RM 72.74," complicates this since it contains "GST" yet still holds the real total value, so I need to make sure my exclusion logic doesn't accidentally filter out the correct line.

Continuing through the other lines - "Rounding Adjustment RM .01", "Rounding RM 72.75", "CASH RM 100.00", "CHANGE RM 27.25" - none clearly fit the TOTAL/AMOUNT pattern once GST and change lines are excluded, so I should probably just run OCR and check empirically rather than guessing further. My best guess remains 72.74 as the Total Sales figure.

Continuing down the line items, neither "Rounding RM 72.75" nor "CASH RM 100.00" matches a TOTAL/AMOUNT keyword, and CHANGE is explicitly excluded, so nothing lines up — meaning my interpretation of the matching logic must be off. I'm reconsidering whether exclusion keywords should be checked by "contains" rather than "starts with," which would explain why the GST line gets skipped even though it has "Total" in it.

Right, so the priority order goes GRAND TOTAL first, then TOTAL RM variants, then TOTAL AMOUNT, then more generic TOTAL/AMOUNT/DUE keywords, with a fallback to grab the last number on the next line if the amount is split across lines. And lines with SUBTOTAL, TAX, GST, SST, DISCOUNT, or CH should be excluded so they don't get mistaken for the actual total.

I'm hitting an edge case though -- for receipt_0151, "Total Sales (Inclusive GST) RM 72.74" gets skipped because it contains GST, and "Rounding RM 72.75" doesn't have a total keyword either, so nothing matches. I suspect my OCR reading of the line might be off, maybe it's actually "GSJ" or some other misread that wouldn't trigger the GST exclusion. I think the best approach is to just run the OCR and see what text actually comes out before trying to patch the logic further.

My plan is a priority-based search: first check for "GRAND TOTAL" while skipping exclusion lines, then fall back to "TOTAL RM" or "TOTAL:", then "TOTAL AMOUNT", then plain "TOTAL" or "AMOUNT" -- since GRAND TOTAL also contains TOTAL as a substring, I need to check most specific patterns first to avoid false matches.

That "Total Sales (Inclusive GST) RM 72.74" line actually gets excluded because it contains GST despite matching TOTAL and TOTAL RM, and the remaining lines like Rounding, CASH, and CHANGE don't match either, leaving no valid match. I'm wondering if OCR might misread "GST" as "GSI" which would break my exclusion logic, so I should just test with actual code.

Adding a date pattern for month names, then moving to extracting totals. Now I'm going through each receipt's filename to map out the actual date found, converting formats like DD/MM/YYYY into standardized YYYY-MM-DD values.

I'm continuing through more date conversions for the remaining receipts, then moving on to verify the expected totals for each filename.

Continuing through the remaining receipts, I'm noting several more cases with ambiguous totals where GST-inclusive amounts conflict with rounded figures, like receipts 0088, 0108, 0124, 0129, 0143, 0151, and 0170, each requiring a judgment call on which total value to extract.

Now I realize the real complication: many receipts show a legitimate "TOTAL" line that already includes GST, meaning my earlier idea to exclude GST-containing lines won't work universally. I need to reconsider the priority ordering of keywords, starting with the most specific like "GRAND TOTAL," then "TOTAL RM" variants, then "TOTAL AMOUNT," and so on down the list.

I'm wondering whether a line like "Rounded Total (RM):" would actually match the substring pattern "TOTAL RM" given the formatting with parentheses and spacing, which affects how I should implement the matching logic across priority tiers.

Looking at receipt_0029 specifically, I'm tracing through the lines: "Total Sales (Excluding GST)" and "Total GST" and "Total Sales (Inclusive of GST)" would all get excluded by the GST/TAX keyword filter, leaving CASH: 94.87 as a candidate, though CASH itself isn't a total keyword so I need to figure out what the correct expected match actually is.

I'm now checking receipt_0082 to see if the same pattern of exclusions applies there, since "Sub Total" and "Total (Incl.GST)" would both be filtered out, which suggests my exclusion logic may be too aggressive and I need a different approach.

Maybe inclusion matching should take priority and only check exclusions when there's no stronger inclusion match, or exclusions should only trigger when the keyword actually labels the amount rather than just appearing in the line. I'm trying to work out the pattern by looking at specific receipt examples to see how "Total Sales" and similar lines actually behave.

I should try a priority-based approach instead: look for GRAND TOTAL first, then specific RM-prefixed total patterns, falling back through a hierarchy of match types rather than trying to exclude GST lines with a single rule.

The real distinction seems to be whether "GST" appears as the primary subject of the line versus a parenthetical qualifier on a sales total - "Total Sales (Inclusive of GST)" should still count as the total, but "Total GST" shouldn't.

This is getting too speculative without seeing actual data. I think the better approach is to just run OCR on the receipts and look at the actual extracted text, then figure out the right heuristics per receipt rather than guessing at expected totals abstractly.

Total Sales Incl GST matches TOTAL at 42.48, then Total After Adj Incl GST matches at 42.50, with the last match being 42.50.

But then I spot "Total promotional saving 11.18" further down, which also contains TOTAL and would match at priority 4, becoming the last match overwriting 100.60 with 11.18 -- which is wrong since the expected answer is 100.60. This reveals a flaw in picking the last match overall; I may need to instead scan top-down and take the first match satisfying the highest priority tier before falling back to lower tiers, though I need to check whether that approach also breaks on receipts like 0029 where an early "Total Q..." line might be a false match.

Now I'm going back through receipt_0185's OCR lines to check item count, total sales including GST, rounding adjustment, and the total after rounding against my matching logic.

I notice "Total promotional saving" is problematic since "SAVING" isn't excluded, so it would wrongly match the generic TOTAL pattern—meaning I need to require TOTAL/AMOUNT matches to be more tightly constrained rather than treated as standalone specific patterns.

Comparing cases, both "Total promotional saving 11.18" and "Total After Rounding 100.60" follow the same "Total X Y amount" shape, so starting-with-keyword alone won't distinguish them—I need either stricter positional rules or a colon/separator requirement to tell these apart.

Instead, I'm considering a positional heuristic: scan top to bottom, collect candidate TOTAL/AMOUNT lines, and stop once hitting a payment line like VISA, CASH, or Change, picking the last valid total found immediately before that payment section.

Testing this against receipts, Receipt_0185's "Total After Rounding 100.60" correctly lands as the last total before VISA, and Receipt_0129's "TOTAL: 41.50" similarly sits right before VISA, confirming the pattern holds across both examples.

For Receipt_0053, "Total Inclusive GST: 10.45" is the last total before CASH, matching the same bottom-up logic. But Receipt_0180 breaks the pattern since there's no CASH/VISA line to anchor on at all—just GST, Amt Due (129.30), and Sub Total, so I'll need to treat "Amt Due" as the target value in cases where no payment method line exists.

Checking Receipt_0088, "Total RM 270.00" clearly matches at priority 2.

For Receipt_0122, I'm weighing whether "Total RM Incl. of GST 40.99" should be excluded since it mentions GST, in which case "Total RM 41.00" becomes the match at priority 2 after the rounding adjustment line.
